question: Why does my laptop keep disconnecting from Wi-Fi every few minutes?
reference_answer: 1. Move closer to the router to rule out signal strength issues. 2. Update your Wi-Fi adapter driver from Device Manager. 3. Disable power-saving mode for the wireless adapter (Device Manager > Network Adapters > Properties > Power Management). 4. Forget the network and reconnect using the correct password. 5. Restart the router by unplugging it for 30 seconds. 6. If the issue persists, check for firmware updates on the router.

question: My computer shows 'No Internet, Secured' on Wi-Fi. How do I fix it?
reference_answer: 1. Restart your router and modem. 2. Run Windows Network Troubleshooter (Settings > Network & Internet > Status > Network Troubleshooter). 3. Flush the DNS cache using 'ipconfig /flushdns' in Command Prompt. 4. Release and renew the IP address with 'ipconfig /release' then 'ipconfig /renew'. 5. Temporarily disable your firewall/antivirus to test for conflicts. 6. If other devices also fail to connect, contact your ISP.

question: How do I connect to a hidden Wi-Fi network?
reference_answer: 1. Open Wi-Fi settings and select 'Add a network' or 'Hidden Network'. 2. Enter the exact network name (SSID) and security type used by the router. 3. Enter the correct password. 4. Save the network so it reconnects automatically next time. 5. If the connection fails, verify the SSID and password with your network administrator.

question: Wi-Fi is connected but pages won't load in the browser. What should I check?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm other devices on the same network can browse normally. 2. Clear your browser cache and cookies. 3. Try a different browser to rule out a browser-specific issue. 4. Flush DNS with 'ipconfig /flushdns' and try changing DNS servers to 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4. 5. Disable VPN or proxy settings temporarily. 6. Restart the router if the problem affects all devices.

question: How can I improve slow Wi-Fi speed at home or in the office?
reference_answer: 1. Restart the router and modem. 2. Move the router to a central, elevated location away from obstructions. 3. Switch to the 5GHz band if available for faster speeds at shorter range. 4. Reduce the number of devices connected simultaneously. 5. Update router firmware. 6. Run a speed test and compare it to your subscribed plan; contact your ISP if results are far below expected.

question: My laptop can't find any Wi-Fi networks at all. What steps should I try?
reference_answer: 1. Ensure Wi-Fi is turned on (check the physical switch or Airplane Mode setting). 2. Restart the laptop. 3. Open Device Manager and check if the wireless adapter shows an error icon; reinstall or update the driver if so. 4. Run the built-in network troubleshooter. 5. Test if other devices detect the network to confirm whether the issue is device-specific or router-specific.

question: How do I reset network settings on Windows when Wi-Fi keeps failing?
reference_answer: 1. Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Status > Network Reset. 2. Confirm the reset; the PC will restart automatically. 3. After restart, reconnect to your Wi-Fi network and re-enter the password. 4. Reinstall any VPN software if it was removed during the reset. 5. If issues continue, update the network adapter driver.

question: Why does my phone connect to Wi-Fi but show a weak signal in one room?
reference_answer: 1. Check the distance and obstacles (walls, appliances) between the device and router. 2. Reposition the router to a more central location. 3. Consider a Wi-Fi extender or mesh system for large spaces. 4. Switch to the 2.4GHz band for better range (at the cost of speed). 5. Update the router firmware to improve signal handling.

question: My printer shows 'Offline' even though it's turned on. How do I fix it?
reference_answer: 1. Check that the printer is powered on and connected via USB or Wi-Fi. 2. Go to Settings > Devices > Printers & Scanners, select the printer, and click 'Set as default'. 3. Right-click the printer and uncheck 'Use Printer Offline' if present. 4. Restart the Print Spooler service (services.msc > Print Spooler > Restart). 5. Reconnect the printer or reinstall the printer driver if the issue persists.

question: Why won't my print jobs leave the queue?
reference_answer: 1. Open the print queue and cancel all stuck jobs. 2. Restart the Print Spooler service from services.msc. 3. Delete any leftover files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS. 4. Restart the printer and computer. 5. Send a new test print to confirm the queue is clear.

question: How do I fix a printer that prints blank pages?
reference_answer: 1. Check ink or toner levels and replace cartridges if low. 2. Run the printer's built-in cleaning utility for the print heads. 3. Confirm you're using the correct paper size and orientation in print settings. 4. Remove and reseat the ink/toner cartridge. 5. Update or reinstall the printer driver if the problem continues.

question: My wireless printer keeps disconnecting from the network. What can I do?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm the printer and computer are on the same Wi-Fi network. 2. Restart the printer and router. 3. Move the printer closer to the router to improve signal strength. 4. Assign a static IP address to the printer to prevent reconnection issues. 5. Update the printer's firmware and reinstall the driver.

question: How do I add a new printer to my computer?
reference_answer: 1. Go to Settings > Devices > Printers & Scanners > Add a printer or scanner. 2. Wait for Windows to detect the printer, or click 'The printer that I want isn't listed' to add it manually by IP address or name. 3. Install the manufacturer's driver if prompted. 4. Print a test page to confirm the setup was successful.

question: Why does my printer say 'paper jam' when there is no visible paper stuck?
reference_answer: 1. Turn off the printer and open all access panels to inspect for small torn paper fragments. 2. Check the paper tray for misaligned or curled paper and reload it properly. 3. Clean the paper rollers with a lint-free cloth to improve paper feed. 4. Restart the printer after clearing any obstructions. 5. If the error persists, consult the manufacturer's manual for hidden jam points.

question: How do I fix garbled or incorrect characters printing on my documents?
reference_answer: 1. Update or reinstall the printer driver, as this is often a driver mismatch issue. 2. Ensure the correct printer model driver is selected, not a generic one. 3. Try printing a different document to see if the issue is document-specific. 4. Restart the print spooler service. 5. Update the printer firmware from the manufacturer's website.

question: My computer has become extremely slow over the past few weeks. What should I check first?
reference_answer: 1. Open Task Manager and check CPU, memory, and disk usage to identify the resource-heavy process. 2. Restart the computer to clear temporary memory buildup. 3. Uninstall unused or unnecessary programs. 4. Run a malware scan using Windows Defender or another trusted antivirus. 5. Disable unnecessary startup programs via Task Manager > Startup tab. 6. Check available disk space and free up storage if it's below 10-15%.

question: How do I reduce the number of programs that launch automatically at startup?
reference_answer: 1. Open Task Manager and go to the 'Startup' tab. 2. Review the list and note the 'Startup impact' column. 3. Right-click any non-essential program and select 'Disable'. 4. Restart the computer to confirm improved boot time. 5. Repeat periodically as new software may re-add itself to startup.

question: My hard drive is almost full and the computer is lagging. How can I free up space?
reference_answer: 1. Run Disk Cleanup (search 'Disk Cleanup' in the Start menu) to remove temporary files. 2. Uninstall unused applications via Settings > Apps. 3. Move large files (videos, photos) to external storage or cloud storage. 4. Empty the Recycle Bin. 5. Disable hibernation if not needed using 'powercfg /hibernate off' in an elevated Command Prompt.

question: How can I tell if malware is causing my system to slow down?
reference_answer: 1. Run a full scan with Windows Defender or a trusted antivirus tool. 2. Check Task Manager for unfamiliar processes consuming high CPU or network usage. 3. Review installed programs for anything you don't recognize and uninstall suspicious entries. 4. Reset your browser settings if you notice unexpected pop-ups or homepage changes. 5. Consider running a secondary malware scanner like Malwarebytes for a second opinion.

question: My computer takes a very long time to boot up. What can I do?
reference_answer: 1. Check the Startup tab in Task Manager and disable unnecessary startup applications. 2. Verify Fast Startup is enabled in Power Options for quicker boot times. 3. Run a disk check using 'chkdsk /f' to rule out drive errors. 4. Consider upgrading to an SSD if you're still using a traditional hard drive. 5. Update the operating system and drivers to the latest versions.

question: Why does my laptop overheat and slow down during heavy use?
reference_answer: 1. Ensure vents are not blocked and use the laptop on a hard, flat surface for proper airflow. 2. Clean dust from vents and fans using compressed air. 3. Check Task Manager for processes causing high CPU usage and close unnecessary ones. 4. Update graphics and chipset drivers, which can improve thermal management. 5. Consider a cooling pad if overheating persists during demanding tasks.

question: How do I check which applications are using the most memory on my PC?
reference_answer: 1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc). 2. Click the 'Memory' column header to sort processes by memory usage. 3. Identify high-usage applications and close ones you don't need running. 4. Consider uninstalling memory-heavy applications you rarely use. 5. Add more RAM if the system consistently runs near full memory capacity.

question: My browser is very slow and sometimes freezes. How can I speed it up?
reference_answer: 1. Clear the browser cache, cookies, and browsing history. 2. Disable or remove unnecessary browser extensions. 3. Update the browser to the latest version. 4. Close unused tabs, as each open tab consumes memory. 5. Try disabling hardware acceleration in browser settings if freezing continues.

question: I forgot my Windows login password. How can I regain access to my account?
reference_answer: 1. On the login screen, click 'I forgot my password' if using a Microsoft account. 2. Follow the prompts to verify your identity via email or phone. 3. Set a new password and sign back in. 4. If using a local account with no reset option, use a password reset disk if you created one previously, or contact IT support for an administrator reset.

question: How do I reset my company email account password?
reference_answer: 1. Go to the company's password reset portal (usually linked from the login page). 2. Enter your username or email address. 3. Verify your identity using the registered phone number, personal email, or security questions. 4. Create a new password that meets the company's complexity requirements. 5. If self-service reset fails, contact the IT helpdesk to have your password reset manually.

question: My account is locked after too many failed password attempts. What should I do?
reference_answer: 1. Wait 15-30 minutes, as many systems automatically unlock accounts after a cooldown period. 2. Use the 'Forgot Password' or 'Unlock Account' link if available. 3. Verify your identity through the registered recovery method. 4. If the account remains locked, contact IT support to have it manually unlocked. 5. Once unlocked, update your password to something memorable but secure.

question: What makes a strong password when resetting my credentials?
reference_answer: 1. Use at least 12 characters combining uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. 2. Avoid common words, names, or easily guessed sequences like '123456'. 3. Don't reuse passwords across multiple accounts. 4. Consider using a passphrase (a memorable sentence) for both strength and ease of recall. 5. Use a password manager to generate and store complex passwords securely.

question: How do I set up two-factor authentication after resetting my password?
reference_answer: 1. Log in to your account settings and locate the 'Security' or 'Two-Factor Authentication' section. 2. Choose a method: authenticator app, SMS code, or email code. 3. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app if selected, or enter your phone number for SMS codes. 4. Save the backup codes provided in a safe place. 5. Test the login process to confirm 2FA is working correctly.

question: I reset my password but I'm still unable to log in. What should I check?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm Caps Lock is off, as passwords are case-sensitive. 2. Make sure you're entering the updated password, not the old one from memory or a saved browser autofill. 3. Clear the browser's saved credentials and try again manually. 4. Check if your account requires additional verification (2FA code). 5. If the problem persists, contact IT support to verify the account status.

question: How often should I be required to change my work password?
reference_answer: 1. Most organizations enforce a password change every 60-90 days for security compliance. 2. Check your company's IT security policy for the exact requirement. 3. You'll typically receive an automatic reminder a few days before expiration. 4. If you receive an expiration warning, reset it promptly through the self-service portal to avoid being locked out. 5. Avoid reusing your last several passwords, as most systems block repeats.

question: I can't log into my email account even though I'm using the correct password. What's wrong?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm there is no ongoing service outage by checking the provider's status page. 2. Double-check for typos, extra spaces, or Caps Lock being on. 3. Try logging in from a different browser or device to rule out local issues. 4. Clear browser cache and cookies. 5. Use the 'Forgot Password' option to reset your credentials if login continues to fail. 6. Contact IT support if the account may have been locked for security reasons.

question: Why am I not receiving any new emails in my inbox?
reference_answer: 1. Check your internet connection to confirm you're online. 2. Verify the mailbox isn't full by checking your storage quota. 3. Check spam/junk folders in case emails are being misfiled. 4. Review any mail filters or rules that might be redirecting incoming messages. 5. Confirm the mail server settings (IMAP/POP/SMTP) haven't changed. 6. Contact IT support if the issue affects multiple users, indicating a server-side problem.

question: How do I configure my email account on Outlook using IMAP settings?
reference_answer: 1. Open Outlook and go to File > Add Account. 2. Enter your email address and select 'Manual setup or additional server types'. 3. Choose IMAP and enter the incoming server (e.g., imap.yourdomain.com, port 993, SSL) and outgoing server (e.g., smtp.yourdomain.com, port 587, TLS). 4. Enter your username and password. 5. Test the account settings and finish setup.

question: My sent emails are bouncing back with a delivery failure error. What should I do?
reference_answer: 1. Check the recipient's email address for typos. 2. Read the bounce-back message for the specific error code (e.g., mailbox full, address not found). 3. Confirm your outgoing mail server (SMTP) settings are correct. 4. Check if your account has been flagged for spam-like sending behavior. 5. Try resending after a short wait, or contact the recipient through another channel to confirm their address.

question: Why can't I access my email on my phone but it works fine on my computer?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm the phone has an active internet or Wi-Fi connection. 2. Delete and re-add the email account in the phone's mail app using the correct server settings. 3. Check if two-factor authentication requires an app-specific password for mobile access. 4. Update the mail app to the latest version. 5. Restart the phone and try logging in again.

question: How do I recover accidentally deleted emails?
reference_answer: 1. Check the 'Deleted Items' or 'Trash' folder first, as items are often recoverable there. 2. If not found, check 'Recoverable Items' or 'Archive' folders depending on your email client. 3. For Outlook/Exchange accounts, use the 'Recover Deleted Items' feature. 4. Act quickly, since many systems permanently purge deleted items after 30 days. 5. Contact IT support for backend mailbox recovery if the email is critical and no longer visible.

question: My email is stuck showing 'Sending...' and never completes. How do I fix it?
reference_answer: 1. Check your internet connection stability. 2. Confirm the attachment size doesn't exceed the provider's limit (commonly 25MB). 3. Restart the email application or refresh the webmail page. 4. Clear the Outbox and try resending the message. 5. Switch networks (e.g., from Wi-Fi to mobile data) to rule out a local connectivity issue.

question: I get an error saying 'Installation failed' when trying to install new software. What can I try?
reference_answer: 1. Run the installer as Administrator (right-click > Run as administrator). 2. Temporarily disable antivirus software, which can sometimes block installers. 3. Ensure you have enough free disk space for the installation. 4. Download the installer again in case the original file was corrupted. 5. Check Windows Update for pending updates that might be blocking installation. 6. Review the installer's error log for a specific error code and search the vendor's support site.

question: Why does my software installation get stuck at a certain percentage and never finish?
reference_answer: 1. Wait a few extra minutes, as some installations pause during background processes. 2. Check Task Manager to confirm the installer process isn't frozen (End Task and restart if needed). 3. Disable antivirus and firewall temporarily during installation. 4. Free up disk space if storage is nearly full. 5. Download a fresh copy of the installer in case of file corruption.

question: I'm getting a 'missing DLL file' error when installing or running a program. How do I fix this?
reference_answer: 1. Reinstall the application, as this often restores missing DLL files automatically. 2. Install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable package, a common source of missing DLLs. 3. Run Windows Update to ensure system files are current. 4. Use the System File Checker tool ('sfc /scannow' in an elevated Command Prompt) to repair corrupted system files. 5. Avoid downloading DLL files individually from untrusted websites, as this can introduce malware.

question: How do I fix 'insufficient permissions' errors during software installation?
reference_answer: 1. Right-click the installer and select 'Run as administrator'. 2. Confirm your Windows user account has administrator privileges (Settings > Accounts). 3. Temporarily disable User Account Control (UAC) if permitted by policy, then re-enable it after installation. 4. Check with IT support if you're on a managed/corporate device, as installation rights may be restricted by policy. 5. Install from a local admin account if available.

question: Why does my software say it's incompatible with my operating system?
reference_answer: 1. Check the software's system requirements against your OS version (Settings > System > About). 2. Update your operating system to the latest version if it's outdated. 3. Look for a version of the software built specifically for your OS. 4. Try running the installer in Compatibility Mode (right-click installer > Properties > Compatibility). 5. Consider using a virtual machine if the software absolutely requires an unsupported OS.

question: My antivirus keeps blocking or deleting a program I'm trying to install. What should I do?
reference_answer: 1. Verify the software is from a legitimate, trusted source before proceeding. 2. Check your antivirus quarantine and restore the file if you trust the source. 3. Add an exception/exclusion for the installer in your antivirus settings. 4. Temporarily disable real-time protection during installation, then re-enable it immediately after. 5. Contact IT support before overriding antivirus on a company device.

question: How do I completely uninstall a program that failed to install correctly, so I can retry?
reference_answer: 1. Go to Settings > Apps > Installed Apps and uninstall the partially installed program. 2. Use the vendor's official removal tool if available, since some software leaves leftover files. 3. Delete any leftover folders in Program Files or AppData related to the software. 4. Clean the registry using a trusted tool if you're comfortable doing so, or skip this step if unsure. 5. Restart the computer before attempting the installation again.

question: My computer suddenly shows a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) with a stop code. What should I do first?
reference_answer: 1. Write down the exact stop code shown on the blue screen (e.g., MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL). 2. Restart the computer and see if it boots normally. 3. Check Windows Update for pending updates and install them. 4. Update graphics and chipset drivers, a common cause of BSODs. 5. Run 'sfc /scannow' and 'chkdsk /f' to check for corrupted files or disk errors. 6. Search the specific stop code online for targeted troubleshooting steps.

question: How do I find the cause of a recent Blue Screen crash using Windows tools?
reference_answer: 1. Open Event Viewer (search in the Start menu) and navigate to Windows Logs > System. 2. Look for 'Critical' or 'Error' events around the time of the crash. 3. Note the associated error code or faulting driver name. 4. Use the Reliability Monitor (search 'View reliability history') for a simplified crash timeline. 5. Search the identified driver or error code for manufacturer-specific fixes.

question: My PC keeps blue-screening with a 'DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL' error. What does this mean and how do I fix it?
reference_answer: 1. This typically indicates a driver is trying to access memory improperly. 2. Boot into Safe Mode and check Device Manager for drivers with warning icons. 3. Update or roll back the most recently installed driver, especially graphics or network drivers. 4. Run Windows Update to ensure all drivers are current. 5. Use Driver Verifier (advanced tool) if the faulty driver isn't obvious, but only if comfortable with advanced troubleshooting.

question: How can I boot into Safe Mode to troubleshoot a Blue Screen issue?
reference_answer: 1. If the PC won't boot normally, force shutdown three times during startup to trigger Automatic Repair. 2. Select 'Advanced Options' > 'Troubleshoot' > 'Advanced Options' > 'Startup Settings' > 'Restart'. 3. After restart, press 4 (or F4) to boot into Safe Mode. 4. In Safe Mode, uninstall recently added software or drivers suspected of causing the crash. 5. Restart normally to see if the issue is resolved.

question: Could faulty RAM cause Blue Screen errors, and how do I test for it?
reference_answer: 1. Yes, faulty or failing RAM is a common cause of random BSODs. 2. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (search 'Windows Memory Diagnostic' in the Start menu) and restart to test. 3. Alternatively, use MemTest86 for a more thorough overnight test. 4. If errors are found, try reseating the RAM modules or testing each stick individually in different slots. 5. Replace any RAM module that consistently fails the test.

question: My computer blue-screens only when I'm playing games or doing graphics-intensive tasks. Why?
reference_answer: 1. Update your graphics card driver to the latest version from the manufacturer's website. 2. Check the GPU temperature using monitoring software, as overheating can trigger crashes. 3. Clean dust from fans and vents to improve cooling. 4. Verify the power supply provides adequate wattage for the graphics card. 5. Run a stress test to confirm whether the GPU is the source of instability.

question: How do I recover my files if my PC won't start due to repeated Blue Screens?
reference_answer: 1. Boot from a Windows installation USB and select 'Repair your computer' instead of installing. 2. Use the Advanced Startup options to access Command Prompt and copy files to an external drive using 'xcopy' or 'robocopy'. 3. Alternatively, remove the hard drive and connect it to another computer as an external drive to retrieve files. 4. Once files are backed up, proceed with System Restore or a clean OS reinstall. 5. Contact IT support if data recovery software is required for a corrupted drive.

question: My VPN won't connect while working from home. What troubleshooting steps should I follow?
reference_answer: 1. Confirm your internet connection is working outside the VPN. 2. Restart the VPN client application. 3. Verify your VPN credentials haven't expired or need a password reset. 4. Check for VPN client software updates. 5. Try a different VPN server location if available. 6. Contact IT support if the VPN server itself may be down.

question: How do I fix a frozen application that isn't responding?
reference_answer: 1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc). 2. Select the unresponsive application and click 'End Task'. 3. Reopen the application to see if it functions normally. 4. Check for and install any pending updates for the application. 5. Restart the computer if multiple applications are freezing, which may indicate a system-level issue.

question: My external monitor isn't being detected by my laptop. How do I troubleshoot this?
reference_answer: 1. Check that the video cable (HDMI/DisplayPort/USB-C) is firmly connected on both ends. 2. Press Windows + P to select a display mode (Extend/Duplicate). 3. Update your graphics driver. 4. Try a different cable or port to rule out a hardware fault. 5. Test the monitor with another device to confirm it's working correctly.

question: How do I free up storage space warnings on a work laptop?
reference_answer: 1. Run Disk Cleanup to remove temporary and system files. 2. Move large files to a network drive or cloud storage like OneDrive. 3. Uninstall unused applications. 4. Empty the Recycle Bin. 5. Check for large hidden files using Storage Settings (Settings > System > Storage).

question: My keyboard or mouse suddenly stopped working. What should I check?
reference_answer: 1. Check the physical connection (USB cable or wireless receiver) and try a different USB port. 2. Replace batteries if using a wireless device. 3. Update or reinstall the device driver in Device Manager. 4. Test the device on another computer to confirm it isn't a hardware fault. 5. Restart the computer to reset device connections.
